title: A quieter bot is a better bot
label: SOFTWARE · FIELD NOTE 01
description: On-demand weather and bounded background work.
body:
Useful automation should leave a little room for everyone else. A group-chat bot is no exception.

Fetch when there is a reason

A weather binding is a preference, not a reason to query every provider forever. The bot fetches a region when someone asks, when a greeting needs it, or when an explicitly configured notification is due. A short per-region cache serves nearby requests; a per-region lock prevents simultaneous requests from repeating the same work.

Keep slow work off the conversation path

Research, video metadata and image recognition can take longer than an ordinary message. Independent jobs, concurrency bounds and time budgets let those tasks finish without making unrelated groups wait. A model listing alone does not prove a model can answer: successful ordinary responses build a preference queue instead.

Collect less, preserve better

A picture is not necessarily a sticker. Explicit sticker metadata and actual GIF headers are stronger evidence than a word in a CDN URL. Oversized non-GIF candidates can be quarantined with their original bytes and index backed up.

These are notes about the project, not a claim that every provider or network failure has been eliminated.

Read the public bot source ↗

title: What survives in a hardware archive?
label: HARDWARE · FIELD NOTE 02
description: Recovering technical sources without overstating a prototype's capabilities.
body:
An old project folder is a record of a process, not automatically a working product. Recovery starts with that distinction.

Keep the parts that can be understood

The fire-rescue vehicle archive retains an ESP32-CAM camera subsystem, infrared remote notes and reviewed CAD drawings. It is not a complete, validated autonomous vehicle. Navigation, chassis and pump behavior cannot be inferred from a camera sketch.

Separate configuration from source

Network credentials belong in a private configuration header. A public example shows the required names without real Wi-Fi information. CAD author metadata and unrelated documents are not necessary to understand the technical export.

Test the claim you can actually test

Offline checks validate archive structure, protocol constants and source relationships. They do not establish that a board package compiles or that hardware behaves safely. Those need build and bench-testing stages. The recovered recording setup sits inside a successful Wi-Fi branch; documenting that limitation is better than repeating an old claim about offline recording.

Explore the recovered subsystem ↗

title: A public map, with private boundaries
label: SOFTWARE · FIELD NOTE 03
description: Shareable recommendations without private bot records.
body:
A public recommendation invites someone to explore a place, not inspect another person's private records.

Start with an explicit public feed

The atlas imports venue names, cities, public addresses, coordinates, categories and original article links from CacheTide's published food-map JSON. Reviews, ratings, photographs, companions and personal comments are not copied. Each place links back to its original source.

Make the boundary structural

This website has a separate repository and deployment. It does not read weather bindings, QQ identifiers, profiles, private maps, chats or stickers. The public updater uses one fixed HTTPS feed once daily, not on every page visit.

Coordinates have a context

The source uses GCJ-02. Amap links retain those coordinates. The optional OpenStreetMap view uses an approximate WGS84 conversion: a discovery aid, not a surveying or navigation instrument. For precision, check the venue in its original map service.

The site never requests your location. The venue list works without interactive tiles.

Open the food atlas →

title: A small site, with clear boundaries
label: PRIVACY & SOURCES
description: What this website publishes and where its data comes from.
body:
No accounts, advertising analytics, or private bot records.

What is public

The notebook contains technical project summaries. The food atlas imports only venue facts and source links from CacheTide's public feed. Original business and city names remain unchanged. A recommendation does not establish that a venue is still open; check its source before travelling.

What stays private

No QQ lists, weather locations, profiles, chats, private maps, API keys, screenshots or sticker databases are imported. This deployment has no write API and does not connect to the home computer.

Your browser

A theme preference may be stored locally. The site does not request geolocation. Loading the optional interactive map contacts OpenStreetMap tile servers, which receive normal connection data such as your IP address and referrer. The list works without tiles. Hosting providers may process operational access logs under their own policies.

Attribution and corrections

Layout inspiration: CacheTide's A Little Inn by the Clouds. The design and notes here are independent; no blog theme, photographs, full articles or ratings were copied. Food source: the public food-map JSON. Interactive map display uses Leaflet and OpenStreetMap.

For a correction or removal request, open a repository issue. Do not post credentials or private contact details.
